incidents.victim: Organizations with exposed OpenLM API endpoints
incidents.vector: Automated scanning for unauthenticated OpenLM inference endpoints; stolen capacity aggregated under a criminal API that uses accumulated AI compute to accelerate further scanning, creating a self-reinforcing growth loop
incidents.impact: Stolen AI inference capacity resold commercially; organizations incur unreported costs and lose proprietary model access; SANS ISC warns all LLM endpoints must require authentication

incidents.victim: Organizations running self-hosted GitLab instances
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0) unauthenticated path traversal in the repository commit API allows any file on the server to be read in a single HTTP request; no credentials required
incidents.impact: Internet-wide probing observed within days of patch release; CISA added to KEV catalog; self-hosted GitLab operators face imminent exploitation leading to source code, secret, and credential exposure; CVE-2026-87719 (CVSS 9.9 Duo Chat prompt injection) also patched

incidents.victim: US AI model developers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, xAI)
incidents.vector: Industrial-scale knowledge distillation: DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI systematically queried US frontier AI models at high volume to extract capabilities and training signals into competing Chinese models; campaign ongoing since late 2024
incidents.impact: NSA/CISA/FBI joint advisory AA26-251A issued; likely conducted with Chinese government awareness; direct threat to US AI technological leadership; affected models include Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok

incidents.victim: US and Canadian driver's license holders (IDScan.net breach)
incidents.vector: Covert long-term intrusion into Louisiana-based identity verification company IDScan.net; attackers continuously exfiltrated driver's license records for over a year; database sold via 'Nexus' dark web service
incidents.impact: 153M+ US and Canadian driver's licenses exposed (~63% of all US licenses); data verified genuine including records of senior US government officials; FBI investigating; fresh data still being added at ~400,000 records/day; national security implications as adversary intelligence services can cross-reference with other stolen datasets

incidents.victim: US defense contractors, NGOs, aerospace companies, Southeast Asian governments
incidents.attacker: China — state intelligence (Ministry of State Security) and affiliated espionage groups
incidents.vector: Four China-aligned espionage groups used a shared 'BlueMoon' exploit kit chaining two Chrome V8 zero-days (CVE-2026-85046, CVE-2026-87491) with Windows ALPC escalation (CVE-2026-85880) to achieve full system compromise; AI reportedly accelerated weaponization of the publicly disclosed Chromium patch within the 4-week gap before stable Chrome release
incidents.impact: US defense contractors, NGOs, commodity traders, aerospace companies, and Southeast Asian governments targeted since late August; malicious Chrome extension disguised as Google Gemini deployed for credential theft and browser surveillance; ShadowPad backdoor installed at US aerospace targets; exploit kit expected to proliferate to additional state and criminal actors

incidents.victim: Organizations using Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center
incidents.attacker: Multiple — Russia-linked military intelligence, criminal ransomware operators, and unattributed actors
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass) combined with CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3 low-privilege login) in Cisco Secure FMC; three separate threat clusters identified exploiting the same vulnerability chain
incidents.impact: Russia-linked cluster (UAT-11823) deployed Cyclops Blink malware previously associated with GRU military intelligence; criminal cluster (UAT-11988) deployed Qilin ransomware; third cluster conducted webshell deployment and credential theft; CISA added to KEV catalog

incidents.victim: Organizations running unpatched Windows (22,000+ Exchange servers exposed)
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-81963 (Windows Update Stack EoP, CVSS 7.8) and CVE-2026-85880 (Windows ALPC EoP, CVSS 7.8) as privilege escalation steps in multi-stage intrusion chains; both exploited in the wild before September 8 Patch Tuesday
incidents.impact: Both CVEs confirmed actively exploited; CVE-2026-81963 used as first step in ransomware kill chains; 22,000+ Exchange servers remain unpatched per Nightwing research; federal agencies given until September 22 to remediate; part of record 974-CVE Patch Tuesday release

incidents.victim: Enterprise organizations (Microsoft Teams users)
incidents.vector: Attackers impersonate IT help desk staff via Microsoft Teams voice calls and chat to social-engineer users into installing remote access tools or Node.js-based backdoors; lateral movement proceeds to domain controllers
incidents.impact: Domain controller compromise enables full-network ransomware deployment; Microsoft assesses as active pre-ransomware campaign targeting multiple organizations; pattern consistent with established ransomware affiliate tradecraft

incidents.victim: Enterprise Microsoft 365 users
incidents.vector: Attacker-in-the-middle phishing pages using fake passkey enrollment lures capture session tokens; Microsoft Graph API used for post-compromise reconnaissance; SharePoint and OneDrive data exfiltrated
incidents.impact: Cloud identity and data theft targeting enterprise Microsoft 365 tenants; active since May 2026 with ongoing campaigns; session token theft bypasses MFA; victims believe they are improving their security posture while being compromised

incidents.victim: Large enterprise (unnamed)
incidents.vector: Criminal actors deployed frontier AI agents to autonomously execute over 50 MITRE ATT&CK techniques sequentially; AI agents navigated the full kill chain from initial access to ransomware deployment, hijacking cloud AI infrastructure mid-attack as an additional offensive platform
incidents.impact: Entire enterprise compromised in under 10 hours; demonstrates AI enabling attack velocity previously requiring specialist red teams; marks a documented threshold in adversarial AI capability against enterprise targets

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government organization
incidents.vector: ClearFake fake browser update social engineering delivering Amatera infostealer; NetSupport Manager deployed as persistent backdoor with command-and-control servers located in Russia
incidents.impact: Ukrainian government network compromised; credentials and sensitive data stolen via Amatera infostealer; persistent espionage access established via NetSupport Manager C2 infrastructure in Russia

incidents.victim: Healthcare, manufacturing, government, and education organizations with China operations
incidents.vector: Trojanized legitimate software installers (Zoom, VPN clients) distributed via phishing targeting the China-based operations of multinational corporations; attributed to Silver Fox/Yinhu threat cluster with moderate confidence China state link
incidents.impact: Remote access trojans installed at organizations' China facilities enabling persistent espionage access; healthcare, manufacturing, government, and education sectors targeted; multinationals' sensitive operations and IP at risk

incidents.victim: Mexican government and transportation sector; Brazilian financial sector
incidents.vector: AI-assisted campaigns using living-off-the-land techniques; Mexico campaign leveraged NextChat LLM tools for reconnaissance and targeting; Brazil campaign deployed custom RATs with SockTz SOCKS5 proxy for covert command-and-control
incidents.impact: Government and transportation organizations in Mexico and financial sector targets in Brazil breached; AI tooling enabling more evasive attack patterns that evade standard detection; assessed as ongoing campaigns expanding across Latin America

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem users (global)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — supply chain (Australian nationals arrested)
incidents.vector: Malicious code embedded in open-source software packages using Shai-Hulud self-propagating worm that automatically spread across interconnected package repositories to maximize reach before detection
incidents.impact: Unknown number of downstream users exposed to supply chain malware; two suspects arrested by Australian Federal Police; self-propagating mechanism represents new automation capability in open-source package compromise

incidents.victim: US consumers and investors (pig butchering / romance scam victims)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — fraud operations (Southeast Asian criminal syndicates)
incidents.vector: Romance baiting and pig butchering investment fraud operated by Southeast Asian criminal organizations; victims gradually groomed then convinced to invest in fraudulent cryptocurrency platforms before accounts are drained
incidents.impact: $12.7B in suspicious digital asset transactions reported to FinCEN; operations backed by transnational criminal organizations linked to human trafficking; FinCEN advisory issued to US financial sector to enhance monitoring

incidents.victim: French notary offices (500+ firms, 7% of the national sector)
incidents.vector: Multi-year phishing-based network intrusions establishing persistent deep access; attackers silently modified wire transfer details within notary transaction workflows over 4 years; France's ANSSI spent 2 years working behind the scenes to remediate
incidents.impact: €35M+ stolen from 500+ notary offices across France; investigators could not rule out forged legal documents (marriages, real estate deeds); national notary regulator overhauled procedures requiring physical presence for financial transactions and banning email for banking details

incidents.victim: JetBrains Cadence cloud LLM training platform and customers
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in JetBrains' own TeamCity CI/CD servers as initial access vector; lateral movement to the Cadence cloud LLM training platform and customer-hosted workloads
incidents.impact: Customer source code and credentials stored in Cadence instances likely stolen; AI model training data and artifacts at risk; breach took place in August and was contained

incidents.victim: US and global victims of Xinbi-linked scam and fraud operations
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — cybercrime marketplace (North Korea-connected, Chinese-operated)
incidents.vector: Xinbi Guarantee Chinese-language cybercrime marketplace facilitated pig-butchering fraud, scam center operations, and money laundering including cryptocurrency services used by North Korean state hackers
incidents.impact: $24B in digital asset transactions processed; billions stolen from American victims; OFAC sanctioned Xinbi Guarantee and two associated companies (SafeW Technology, Anwen Technology); marketplace connected to North Korea's cryptocurrency theft money-laundering pipeline

incidents.victim: Organizations using SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances
incidents.vector: Chained CVE-2026-83548 (CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF) and CVE-2026-83549 (CVSS 7.8 OS command injection) achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances at the network edge
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed at disclosure; CISA KEV listed; fifth actively exploited SonicWall vulnerability since late 2025; historically a precursor to ransomware deployment; no attribution or victim count disclosed; vendor urged customers to reimage affected appliances

incidents.victim: US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion targeting ATF's CALEA (Communications Assistance for Law Enforcement Act) lawful interception system; data exfiltrated and published on the group's dark web leak site
incidents.impact: 6.3GB of law enforcement data briefly published including names, phone numbers, IP addresses of investigation targets, and mobile device forensic data; ATF Director confirmed investigating CALEA breach; sensitive counterintelligence and investigative data compromised

incidents.victim: Nutex Health (27-hospital system across 12 states)
incidents.vector: Gentlemen ransomware-as-a-service group (Russian-speaking, former Qilin affiliate, operating since September 2025) breached network, exfiltrated patient and financial data, and issued extortion demand threatening public disclosure
incidents.impact: Patient, employee, provider, and confidential financial data stolen from $427M-revenue hospital network; class action lawsuit filed; Gentlemen group has claimed 350+ attacks in 2026 including shutting down AnMed nonprofit medical system and forcing facility closures

incidents.victim: Organizations using JFrog Artifactory
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-82329 (CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass) allows unauthenticated creation of Artifactory admin tokens; exploited within 3 days of August 28 public disclosure
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed; CISA KEV listed; admin token theft enables full artifact repository access and potential poisoning of software build pipelines; downstream supply chain risk for all consumers of affected repositories

incidents.victim: Stadtwerke Landsberg (Bavarian municipal utility)
incidents.vector: Ransomware encryption of central IT network overnight September 1; utility disconnected affected systems, activated crisis team, and engaged external cybersecurity specialists
incidents.impact: Corporate IT systems encrypted; customer service severely limited; potential exposure of customer personal and banking data; public utilities (electricity, water) reported unaffected; forensic investigation ongoing

incidents.victim: McKesson (distributes ~1/3 of North American pharmaceuticals, $403B revenue)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters exploited identity and access management weaknesses to compromise cloud-hosted third-party applications; credential abuse mimicked normal support workflows, evading detection for 4 days (August 21-25)
incidents.impact: Oncology, multispecialty, and medical-surgical customer data stolen from the distributor of roughly one-third of all North American pharmaceuticals; $55M+ ransom demanded; potential supply chain disruption risk to healthcare sector

incidents.victim: Berlin city government (urban development and transport ministries)
incidents.vector: Employee deceived by ClickFix fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA, installing malware; Rhysida ransomware deployed; 5.79TB of data exfiltrated August 7-12 before discovery and isolation on August 14
incidents.impact: 5.79TB stolen including 46,500 contracts, emails, phone numbers, passwords, and classified documents; Berlin refused $2.3M ransom demand; two ministries disrupted three weeks before September 20 regional elections; election systems separately assessed as secure

incidents.victim: Virtualizor/Softaculous VPS hosting management platform users
incidents.vector: BGP hijack of Softaculous IP space (162.55.80.0/24) via rogue ASN for 33 hours; attacker obtained forged TLS certificate and served malicious Virtualizor software updates from a cloned site
incidents.impact: Users downloading Virtualizor updates during the 33-hour window likely received malware; payment data potentially stolen; victim scope undetermined as malicious traffic bypassed vendor logging infrastructure; Virtualizor is widely used by commercial VPS hosting providers
